plan: This is a second-price auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win (not my own bid), bidding exactly my value of $25 ensures I win whenever it's profitable (value exceeds the price I'd pay) and never overpay. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value if the second-highest bid exceeds $25, while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, the optimal strategy is to bid my true value of $25.

This is a second-price auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. If I bid exactly my value ($17), I ensure I never overpay (since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win) and I never miss out on profitable wins (since winning at any price below $17 is profitable). Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth to me, while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, my optimal bid is $17.

This is a second-price auction where bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding above my value adds risk of overpaying relative to my value if I'm not truly the highest, while bidding below risks losing profitable opportunities. Bidding exactly $39 ensures I win whenever profitable (when others bid less than $39) and never overpay since I only pay the second-highest bid.
